items.name: Port Au Prince
items.description: A vibrant Haitian-inspired rum punch bursting with pineapple and spice.
items.story: Martin Cate's take on this classic draws from mid-century tiki traditions, evoking the exotic ports of Haiti where rum flowed freely. Created as a nod to the island's vibrant culture, the name references Port-au-Prince, Haiti's capital. Bartenders love telling guests it's a 'sailor's delight'—strong enough to weather any storm but bright enough to make you forget the waves. A perfect introduction to allspice dram's warm complexity.
items.instructions: Shake all ingredients with ice. Strain into a rocks glass filled with crushed ice. Garnish with a pineapple spear and mint sprig.

items.name: Halekulani Cocktail
items.description: A refined 1930s Waikiki classic blending bourbon with tropical brightness.
items.story: Originating from the House Without a Key lounge at the Halekulani Hotel in Waikiki during the 1930s, this elegant sipper was adapted by Martin Cate from Beachbum Berry's research. It captures the golden era of Hawaiian tourism when Hollywood stars escaped to paradise. The name means 'House of Heaven'—a fitting tribute. Guests always smile when you mention it was a favorite of those seeking sophistication amid the tiki boom.
items.instructions: Shake with ice and double-strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with an edible orchid.

items.name: Sidewinder's Fang
items.description: A potent, snake-bite sharp blend of rums and citrus with a venomous kick.
items.story: This Don the Beachcomber classic gets its fierce name from the 'sidewinder'—a deadly desert rattlesnake—symbolizing its sneaky potency. Revived and refined at Smuggler's Cove, it's a golden-era powerhouse. Legend has it Donn Beach created many such 'fangs' to keep Hollywood's elite entertained (and slightly off-balance). Tell guests it's 'one bite and you're hooked'—they'll order another round instantly.
items.instructions: Shake with crushed ice and pour unstrained into a tiki mug. Garnish with mint and a lime wheel.

items.name: Formidable Dragon
items.description: A formidable beast of molasses, honey, and powerful rums.
items.story: Crafted for a 2015 tiki event, this Smuggler's Cove original honors British Admiral Edward Vernon (Old Grog) and naval rum traditions. The 'dragon' refers to its fiery strength and mythical allure. Martin Cate uses it to illustrate tiki's blend of history and theater. Guests love the tale of how it 'breathes fire'—a nod to the potent rum blend that sneaks up like a dragon at sea.
items.instructions: Shake with ice, strain into a glass over crushed ice, top with soda. Garnish with mint and lemon wheel.

items.name: Hana Reviver
items.description: A revitalizing floral and herbal tiki reviver from paradise.
items.story: This Smuggler's Cove creation captures the spirit of Hana, Maui—a hidden paradise. It revives the drinker with bright, restorative notes inspired by Hawaiian botanicals and tiki revival ingenuity. Martin Cate uses it to showcase how modern tiki honors place and history. Tell guests it's 'the cure for whatever ails you after a long sail.'
items.instructions: Shake with ice and strain into a chilled coupe or tiki glass. Garnish with edible flowers and mint.

items.name: Aku Aku
items.description: A mysterious, creamy almond-coconut tiki classic with deep rum character.
items.story: Named after the famous 1930s film and book that popularized Polynesian mystique, this Don the Beachcomber creation was revived by Martin Cate. It captures the escapist fantasy of early tiki—guests feel transported to a hidden South Seas lagoon. The name 'Aku Aku' refers to guardian spirits; bartenders love whispering that one sip summons good fortune (and maybe a second round).
items.instructions: Shake with crushed ice and pour unstrained into a tiki mug. Garnish with mint and pineapple.

items.name: Hawaiian Sunset
items.description: A glowing sunset of pineapple, grenadine, and smooth rums.
items.story: Evoking those magical Hawaiian evenings, this golden-era beauty layers colors like the sky over Waikiki. Adapted at Smuggler's Cove, it's a visual and flavorful stunner. The story always delights guests: 'Watch it change hues just like the islands at dusk.'
items.instructions: Build in a tall glass with crushed ice, layering grenadine at bottom. Garnish with pineapple and cherry.

items.name: Lei Lani Volcano
items.description: A floral eruption of passion fruit, rum, and volcanic spice.
items.story: Modern Smuggler's Cove creation inspired by Hawaiian leis and explosive tiki theatrics. The 'volcano' refers to its layered intensity. Martin Cate uses it to showcase how tiki evolves—beautiful, fragrant, and memorably potent. Guests love the story of it 'erupting' with flavor.
items.instructions: Shake with ice and strain into a tiki glass over crushed ice. Garnish with orchid and mint.

items.name: Tradewinds
items.description: Smooth coconut and apricot winds carrying rich Jamaican rums.
items.story: A 1970s Jamaican-inspired drink revived by Beachbum Berry and polished at Smuggler's Cove. It evokes the steady trade winds that powered sailing ships across the Caribbean. The creamy apricot note makes it a charter favorite—'smooth sailing in a glass.'
items.instructions: Shake with ice and strain over crushed ice. Garnish with lime and a paper umbrella.

items.name: Swizzle Français
items.description: A French-Caribbean swizzle with agricole rum and Chartreuse elegance.
items.story: Martin Cate's modern tribute blending Martinique rhum agricole with herbal French liqueurs. It bridges tiki and classic cocktail worlds. The swizzle technique is pure theater—guests are mesmerized as you spin the drink into a frosty masterpiece.
items.instructions: Build in a Collins glass with crushed ice. Swizzle vigorously. Garnish with mint and nutmeg.

items.name: The Undead Gentleman
items.description: A sophisticated Zombie cousin with absinthe elegance.
items.story: Smuggler's Cove's refined take on the undead tiki legend. It's 'gentlemanly' in balance but still dangerously potent. The story ties back to Donn Beach's wild originals—perfect for telling tales of tiki's rebellious past while serving something polished.
items.instructions: Shake with crushed ice and pour into a tiki mug. Float absinthe. Garnish with mint.

items.name: Don's Own Grog
items.description: Don the Beachcomber's personal grog — bold, honeyed, and refreshingly potent.
items.story: This was Donn Beach's own go-to variation of the classic Navy Grog. Martin Cate revived it as a tribute to the father of tiki. The name honors the man who started it all in the 1930s. Bartenders tell guests it's the drink that kept Donn creative through long Hollywood nights — strong enough to fuel genius, balanced enough to enjoy.
items.instructions: Shake with ice and strain into a rocks glass filled with crushed ice. Garnish with lime wheel and mint.

items.name: Mundo Perdido
items.description: Jeff Berry's lost-world creation of apple brandy and dark rum.
items.story: Created exclusively for Smuggler's Cove by Jeff “Beachbum” Berry in 2009. “Mundo Perdido” (Lost World) evokes forgotten tropical paradises. It's a modern classic that bridges old and new tiki. Guests enjoy hearing how it was designed as a lighter, more approachable tiki drink.
items.instructions: Shake with ice and strain into a coupe or rocks glass. Garnish with lemon twist.

items.name: Twenty Seventy Swizzle
items.description: A high-octane swizzle named for its potent 127-proof rum.
items.story: A modern Smuggler's Cove powerhouse that nods to overproof rum's strength. The name references the 127 proof of the black rum used. It's become legendary for its balance and the theatrical swizzle ritual. Perfect for telling guests it's “strong enough to launch you into the stars.”
items.instructions: Build in a Collins glass with crushed ice and swizzle vigorously. Garnish with mint, nutmeg, and swizzle stick.

items.name: The Dead Reckoning
items.description: A complex navigation of rums, amaro, and citrus precision.
items.story: Smuggler's Cove's modern classic named after the nautical art of dead reckoning. It rewards careful balancing of strong ingredients — much like plotting a course. Martin Cate uses it to illustrate tiki's precision beneath the fun. Tell guests it's the drink that always finds its way home.
items.instructions: Shake with crushed ice and pour unstrained into a tiki mug. Garnish with mint.

items.name: Kaiteur Swizzle
items.description: A Guyanese-inspired powerhouse swizzle honoring mighty falls.
items.story: Inspired by Guyana's spectacular Kaiteur Falls, this bold Demerara swizzle celebrates the power of premium rum. Smuggler's Cove version highlights heritage while delivering refreshing drinkability. The swizzle action mimics cascading water — pure tiki theater.
items.instructions: Build in a tall glass with crushed ice and swizzle well. Garnish with lime and nutmeg.

items.name: Chartreuse Swizzle
items.description: A vibrant green swizzle marrying Chartreuse and island spices.
items.story: Smuggler's Cove's elegant fusion of French herbal tradition with Caribbean swizzle technique. It showcases tiki's willingness to embrace the world's best ingredients. The brilliant color always sparks conversation — 'the jungle comes alive in your glass.'
items.instructions: Build in Collins glass with crushed ice. Swizzle thoroughly. Garnish with mint and lime.

items.name: Port Light
items.description: Trader Vic's bourbon beauty with passion fruit and honey brightness.
items.story: A Trader Vic classic from the golden era, the Port Light showcases bourbon's place in tiki alongside rum. Martin Cate's adaptation highlights its elegant balance. The name evokes a welcoming harbor light — perfect for guiding guests into tiki paradise. It's a favorite for showing that tiki isn't just rum.
items.instructions: Shake with ice and strain into a rocks glass over crushed ice. Garnish with a cherry and orange wheel.

items.name: Demerara Dry Float
items.description: Don the Beachcomber's dry, potent Demerara rum float.
items.story: A Don the Beachcomber original emphasizing the rich, earthy character of Demerara rums. Revived at Smuggler's Cove, it showcases early tiki's love of bold, unadorned rum. The 'dry float' refers to the technique of floating heavier rum on top. Bartenders call it a 'sailor's handshake' — straightforward and strong.
items.instructions: Shake base ingredients with ice and strain into a glass with crushed ice. Float Demerara rum on top. Garnish with lime.

items.name: Mexican El Diablo
items.description: Trader Vic's fiery tequila-ginger devil with lime and cassis.
items.story: A Trader Vic creation that cleverly brings tequila into the tiki fold. The name 'El Diablo' (The Devil) warns of its sneaky heat from ginger beer. Martin Cate includes it as an example of tiki's global influences. Guests always grin when you say it's 'the devil you want to dance with.'
items.instructions: Build in a tall glass with ice. Top with ginger beer. Garnish with lime wheel.

items.name: Singapore Sling
items.description: Trader Vic's tiki-fied version of the classic Singapore Sling.
items.story: Trader Vic adapted this famous Raffles Hotel drink for the American tiki scene. Martin Cate presents it as a bridge between classic cocktails and exotic tiki. The vibrant pink color and layered flavors made it a Hollywood favorite. Tell guests it's the sling that launched a thousand toasts.
items.instructions: Shake with ice and strain into a tall glass over ice. Garnish with cherry and orange.

items.name: Tiki Bowl
items.description: Don the Beachcomber's legendary communal sharing bowl.
items.story: One of Don the Beachcomber's iconic large-format drinks designed for groups. It embodies tiki's communal spirit. Smuggler's Cove version keeps the fun and theater alive. The story of friends passing the bowl around a table is pure tiki magic — ideal for your charter crew or guests.
items.instructions: Blend ingredients with ice and pour into a large bowl. Garnish lavishly with fruit and flowers. Serve with long straws.

items.name: Hurricane
items.description: Trader Vic's powerful passion fruit rum hurricane.
items.story: Trader Vic's take on the New Orleans classic, adapted for tiki with extra rum power. It captures the wild energy of a tropical storm. Martin Cate includes it as a fun, shareable crowd-pleaser. The name guarantees smiles — 'it hits like a hurricane but tastes like paradise.'
items.instructions: Shake with ice and strain into a tall glass over crushed ice. Garnish with orange and cherry.

items.name: Scorpion
items.description: Don the Beachcomber's famous communal Scorpion Bowl.
items.story: A legendary large-format drink from Don the Beachcomber, meant for sharing among friends. The 'scorpion' sting comes from its deceptive strength. Smuggler's Cove keeps the tradition alive for groups. It's the ultimate icebreaker — one bowl, many stories.
items.instructions: Blend with ice and serve in a large bowl. Garnish with flowers and fruit. Share with straws.

items.name: Test Pilot
items.description: Don the Beachcomber's nuanced test pilot — a refined Zombie sibling.
items.story: Don the Beachcomber's original, a slightly more approachable cousin to the Zombie. The name reflects its test-flight potency. Smuggler's Cove version highlights Donn's precision with multiple rums and secret ingredients. It's the drink for guests who want adventure without full blackout.
items.instructions: Shake with crushed ice and pour unstrained. Garnish with mint and cherry.

items.name: Jet Pilot
items.description: Don the Beachcomber's turbo-charged, high-octane Zombie variant.
items.story: Don the Beachcomber's powerful 'jet' version of the Zombie — faster and stronger. Smuggler's Cove adaptation is a favorite for its complexity. The name promises speed and altitude — one sip and you're cleared for takeoff. A legendary drink for adventurous palates.
items.instructions: Flash blend with crushed ice and pour into a tiki mug. Float absinthe. Garnish with mint.

items.name: Doctor Funk
items.description: Don the Beachcomber's mysterious Samoan-inspired absinthe rum drink.
items.story: A Don the Beachcomber classic with roots in Stevenson-era Samoa. The 'Funk' refers to its exotic, slightly mysterious profile. Revived by Smuggler's Cove, it's a refreshing yet eccentric favorite. The story of its Pacific origins always captivates guests around the bar.
items.instructions: Shake and strain into a highball over ice. Top with soda. Garnish with lime.

items.name: Pupule
items.description: Don the Beachcomber's wild 'crazy' multi-rum passion fruit punch.
items.story: A Don the Beachcomber original whose name means 'crazy' in Hawaiian. It perfectly captures the wild, uninhibited spirit of early tiki. Smugglers Cove's version keeps the potent multi-rum profile while ensuring balance. Bartenders love telling guests it's the drink that makes even the most reserved sailor go pupule.
items.instructions: Shake with ice and strain into a tall glass over crushed ice. Garnish with pineapple spear and cherry.

items.name: Captain's Grog
items.description: Trader Vic's hearty captain's rum grog with honey and citrus.
items.story: A Trader Vic staple inspired by naval grog traditions. It honors the captains who navigated the rum trade routes. Smuggler's Cove version is robust yet refined. Guests love the tale of how it kept captains steady through stormy seas — now ideal for BVI anchorages.
items.instructions: Shake with ice and strain over crushed ice. Garnish with lime wheel and mint.

items.name: Merciless Virgin
items.description: A dangerously smooth coconut-rum temptation from Trader Vic's era.
items.story: A playful Trader Vic-style creamy tiki drink with a mischievous name. Smuggler's Cove version is luxuriously balanced. The 'merciless' refers to how quickly it disappears. It's a charter favorite — rich, tropical, and impossible to resist.
items.instructions: Shake vigorously with ice and strain over crushed ice. Garnish with grated nutmeg.

items.name: Hondo Hattie's Jungle Punch
items.description: A legendary large-format jungle punch from Don the Beachcomber.
items.story: One of Don the Beachcomber's famous communal punches, named after a colorful tiki personality. It embodies the theatrical, group-celebration side of tiki. Perfect for sharing stories under the stars in the BVI.
items.instructions: Blend with ice and serve in a large bowl. Garnish extravagantly with fruit and flowers.

items.name: Kahiko Punch
items.description: An ancient-style Hawaiian punch revived by Don the Beachcomber.
items.story: 'Kahiko' means ancient in Hawaiian. This Don the Beachcomber punch draws from early Polynesian communal drinking traditions. Smuggler's Cove version brings it into the modern tiki canon. It's a beautiful reminder that tiki has deep roots.
items.instructions: Shake and strain into a punch bowl or individual glasses over ice. Garnish with tropical fruit.

items.name: Eureka Punch
items.description: A triumphant multi-rum punch from the golden era.
items.story: Don the Beachcomber's celebratory punch — the 'Eureka' moment of discovery. It showcases his mastery of balancing multiple rums and juices. A true crowd-pleaser that feels like a eureka moment with every sip.
items.instructions: Shake and serve in a large format or individual glasses over crushed ice.

items.name: Triumvirate Punch
items.description: A powerful three-rum punch celebrating tiki's ruling triumvirate.
items.story: Named for the three great rum styles working in harmony. A Don the Beachcomber-style communal punch revived at Smuggler's Cove. It represents the holy trinity of tiki rums — light, dark, and aged. Perfect for group toasts on deck.
items.instructions: Blend or shake and serve in a punch bowl with plenty of crushed ice and garnishes.

items.name: Yuletide Punch
items.description: A festive spiced rum punch perfect for holiday or special occasions.
items.story: A seasonal Don the Beachcomber-style punch adapted by Smuggler's Cove for winter tiki celebrations. It brings warm spices to the tropical format. Even in the Caribbean, it's a hit for special charter nights or crossing the equator parties.
items.instructions: Warm or shake and serve in punch glasses. Garnish with orange slices and spices.

items.name: Planter's Punch
items.description: The foundational Jamaican Planter's Punch as interpreted by Don the Beachcomber.
items.story: One of the oldest tiki building blocks, refined by Don the Beachcomber. It showcases how simple ratios of rum, citrus, and sugar created the entire genre. Smuggler's Cove version is the gold standard. Every tiki bartender tells the story of how this drink planted the seeds of the tiki movement.
items.instructions: Shake with ice and strain into a tall glass over crushed ice. Garnish with mint and lime.

items.name: Arrack Punch
items.description: A historic Caribbean arrack punch with island spice and citrus.
items.story: One of the oldest punch styles in the Caribbean rum trade, adapted by Smuggler's Cove from historic recipes. Arrack (often Batavia or local variants) was a staple in early West Indian trade. Martin Cate includes it to show the deep roots of tiki in Caribbean punch culture. A true taste of maritime history.
items.instructions: Shake with ice and strain over crushed ice. Garnish with lime and grated nutmeg.

items.name: El Draque
items.description: The ancient Caribbean precursor to the Mojito, tiki style.
items.story: Named after Sir Francis Drake, this early Caribbean rum-mint-lime drink is one of the ancestors of modern cocktails. Smuggler's Cove version honors its West Indian roots. It's a living piece of maritime history — the drink that powered explorers and pirates alike.
items.instructions: Muddle mint with lime and honey. Add rum and ice, shake, and strain over crushed ice. Garnish with mint.

items.name: Grog
items.description: The original British Naval grog from Caribbean rum rations.
items.story: Admiral Edward Vernon's famous 1740 ration of rum, water, lime, and sugar — the drink that prevented scurvy and powered the Royal Navy in the Caribbean. Don the Beachcomber and Smuggler's Cove elevated it into tiki glory. Every BVI sailor should know this foundational drink.
items.instructions: Build in a glass with ice. Stir and garnish with lime.

items.name: Rum Flip
items.description: A historic Caribbean rum flip with egg and nutmeg.
items.story: An old seafaring drink popular in the Caribbean rum trade. The flip (shaken with egg) was a sailor's fortifying treat. Smuggler's Cove version brings it into tiki with quality rum. It's creamy, rich, and perfect for cooler evenings in the islands.
items.instructions: Shake hard with ice (including egg) and strain into a glass. Garnish with grated nutmeg.

items.name: Caribeño
items.description: A modern Caribbean coconut-rum refresher.
items.story: Smuggler's Cove's contemporary take celebrating everyday Caribbean beach life. Light coconut and bright citrus make it a perfect daytime sipper for the islands. It captures the relaxed, sun-soaked spirit of the West Indies.
items.instructions: Shake with ice and strain over crushed ice. Garnish with lime and coconut flake.

items.name: Monk's Respite
items.description: A contemplative Caribbean herbal rum cooler.
items.story: Smuggler's Cove creation inspired by quiet moments in the islands. It balances herbal liqueurs with bright Caribbean citrus and rum. Named for the peaceful respite it provides — ideal after a long sail or busy charter day.
items.instructions: Shake with ice and strain into a Collins glass over ice. Top with soda if desired.

items.name: The Mastadon
items.description: A massive, powerful Caribbean rum beast.
items.story: A big, bold Smuggler's Cove punch evoking the strength of Caribbean maritime history. Like the mighty creatures of old, it's not for the faint of heart. Perfect for sharing among strong crews or celebrating a successful passage.
items.instructions: Shake and serve in a large format or strong individual glasses over crushed ice.

items.name: Piñata
items.description: A festive Caribbean fruit-filled rum celebration.
items.story: Smuggler's Cove's playful punch inspired by Caribbean fiestas. Like breaking a piñata, it's full of sweet surprises and tropical joy. Ideal for charter parties or special occasions in the islands.
items.instructions: Shake or blend and serve over ice in a festive glass. Garnish with plenty of fruit.

items.name: Bumboat
items.description: A lively Caribbean bumboat rum and coconut drink.
items.story: Inspired by the bustling bum boats that supplied ships in Caribbean ports. Smuggler's Cove version captures the lively, tropical energy of island trade. Creamy coconut with bright citrus and spice — a perfect taste of dockside life.
items.instructions: Shake with ice and strain over crushed ice. Garnish with lime and coconut.

items.name: Callaloo Cooler
items.description: A Trinidadian-inspired herbal green cooler with rum.
items.story: Drawing from Trinidad's famous Callaloo soup and island greenery, this Smuggler's Cove cooler is bright, herbal, and refreshing. It celebrates the fresh, vibrant flavors of the Eastern Caribbean. A wonderful palate cleanser between richer tiki drinks.
items.instructions: Shake with ice and strain into a Collins glass over ice. Top with soda. Garnish with mint.

items.name: Old Fashioned
items.description: The original cocktail — a simple, elegant whiskey drink that started it all.
items.story: First documented in the early 1800s, the Old Fashioned is the drink that gave the word 'cocktail' its meaning. It evolved from the basic spirit-sugar-water-bitters formula. A true American classic that has survived every trend. Bartenders love telling guests it's the grandfather of all mixed drinks — strong, simple, and timeless.
items.instructions: Stir whiskey, sugar, and bitters with ice. Strain over a large ice cube in a rocks glass. Garnish with orange twist.

ingredients.name: Demerara Sugar Cube or Simple Syrup

items.name: Martini
items.description: The epitome of sophistication — crisp gin and vermouth.
items.story: Evolving in the late 19th century from the Martinez, the Martini became the symbol of elegance during the Jazz Age and beyond. Its simplicity hides perfect balance. Whether wet or dry, it remains the king of cocktails. Every great bartender has their own ritual for this timeless icon.
items.instructions: Stir gin and dry vermouth with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe or martini glass. Garnish with olive or lemon twist.

items.name: Manhattan
items.description: A rich, aromatic whiskey and vermouth classic.
items.story: Created in the 1870s at the Manhattan Club in New York, this drink became a favorite of politicians and high society. The perfect marriage of American whiskey and Italian vermouth. It's bold, sophisticated, and endlessly customizable — a true cornerstone of the cocktail canon.
items.instructions: Stir whiskey, sweet vermouth, and bitters with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with cherry.

items.name: Daiquiri
items.description: The perfect Cuban rum, lime, and sugar classic.
items.story: Born in Cuba around 1900 and named after a beach near Santiago, the Daiquiri was popularized by American writers and sailors. Its simplicity is its genius — the ultimate expression of quality rum. Hemingway loved the frozen version, but the shaken classic remains the gold standard.
items.instructions: Shake rum, lime juice, and sugar with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with lime wheel.

items.name: Sidecar
items.description: A refined cognac, orange liqueur, and lemon classic.
items.story: Created in Paris during World War I and named after the motorcycle sidecar of an American officer. It became a symbol of elegance in the 1920s. The perfect balance of rich cognac and bright citrus makes it a timeless favorite for those who appreciate history in a glass.
items.instructions: Shake cognac, triple sec, and lemon juice with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe. Sugar rim optional.

items.name: Whiskey Sour
items.description: The quintessential American whiskey sour.
items.story: Documented in the 1860s, the Whiskey Sour is one of the oldest and most beloved sour cocktails. It traveled the world with sailors and became a staple in bars everywhere. Its perfect balance of sweet, sour, and spirit makes it eternally satisfying.
items.instructions: Shake whiskey, lemon juice, and simple syrup with ice. Strain into a rocks glass over ice or straight up. Garnish with orange and cherry.

items.name: Negroni
items.description: The iconic equal-parts Italian aperitivo.
items.story: Invented in Florence around 1919 when Count Camillo Negroni asked for a stronger Americano. It became a global classic in the 20th century. The perfect bittersweet balance makes it a sophisticated choice before dinner or at sunset.
items.instructions: Stir gin, Campari, and sweet vermouth with ice. Strain over a large ice cube. Garnish with orange twist.

items.name: Boulevardier
items.description: The whiskey Negroni — rich and sophisticated.
items.story: Created in the 1920s for Erskine Gwynne's Paris magazine *The Boulevardier*. A whiskey lover's answer to the Negroni. It gained massive popularity during the modern cocktail renaissance. Bold, bitter, and beautiful — a drink with literary pedigree.
items.instructions: Stir bourbon, Campari, and sweet vermouth with ice. Strain over a large ice cube. Garnish with orange twist.

items.name: Corpse Reviver No. 2
items.description: The famous 'hair of the dog' hangover cure from the Savoy.
items.story: From the 1930 Savoy Cocktail Book, this is the most famous of the Corpse Reviver family. The recipe warns 'four of these taken in swift succession will un-revive the dead.' A perfectly balanced, complex classic that actually works as a morning pick-me-up.
items.instructions: Shake all ingredients with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with orange twist.

items.name: Sazerac
items.description: The official cocktail of New Orleans — rich rye with absinthe rinse.
items.story: Created in the 1830s in New Orleans using Cognac and Peychaud's bitters, later adapted with rye whiskey. It is widely considered America's oldest cocktail. The ritual of the absinthe rinse and the Peychaud's bitters make it a true piece of cocktail history and a sophisticated sipper.
items.instructions: Rinse a chilled rocks glass with absinthe. Stir rye, sugar, and Peychaud's bitters with ice. Strain into the glass. Garnish with lemon twist.

items.name: Vieux Carré
items.description: A rich New Orleans classic with rye, cognac, and Benedictine.
items.story: Created in the 1930s at the Carousel Bar in New Orleans' Hotel Monteleone. Named after the French Quarter (Vieux Carré). It beautifully blends American rye with French cognac and herbal Benedictine — a true melting pot of cocktail history in one glass.
items.instructions: Stir all ingredients with ice. Strain into a rocks glass over ice. Garnish with cherry and lemon twist.

items.name: Last Word
items.description: The equal-parts Prohibition-era gem with chartreuse and maraschino.
items.story: Created around 1916 at the Detroit Athletic Club. It was lost for decades and revived during the modern cocktail renaissance. The perfect harmony of four equal parts makes it a bartender favorite and a shining example of pre-Prohibition ingenuity.
items.instructions: Shake gin, lime juice, maraschino liqueur, and green Chartreuse with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with cherry.

items.name: Bee's Knees
items.description: A bright, honey-sweetened gin sour from the Jazz Age.
items.story: A Prohibition-era favorite (the phrase 'bee's knees' meant 'the best'). Honey was used to mask poor-quality gin during the dry years. Simple, elegant, and delicious — it perfectly captures the spirit of the Roaring Twenties.
items.instructions: Shake gin, lemon juice, and honey syrup with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with lemon twist.

items.name: South Side
items.description: A minty, refreshing gin sour from Chicago speakeasies.
items.story: Popularized in Chicago's South Side speakeasies during Prohibition. The fresh mint makes it incredibly vibrant. It's a direct ancestor of the Mojito and a perfect hot-weather classic that feels right at home in the Caribbean.
items.instructions: Shake gin, lemon juice, and simple syrup with mint. Double-strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with mint sprig.

items.name: French 75
items.description: The sparkling gin-lemon Champagne cocktail named after a WWI gun.
items.story: Created during World War I and named after the powerful French 75mm field gun. It packs a serious punch despite its elegant appearance. A staple at the Savoy and a symbol of celebratory elegance ever since.
items.instructions: Shake gin, lemon juice, and simple syrup with ice. Strain into a flute and top with Champagne. Garnish with lemon twist.

items.name: Tom Collins
items.description: The tall, refreshing gin lemonade of the 19th century.
items.story: Popular since the 1860s, the Tom Collins is a simple, tall gin sour topped with soda. It became a worldwide favorite and inspired many variations. Its refreshing nature makes it perfect for warm-weather sailing and relaxing in the islands.
items.instructions: Shake gin, lemon juice, and simple syrup with ice. Strain into a Collins glass over ice and top with soda. Garnish with lemon wheel and cherry.

items.name: Pisco Sour
items.description: The frothy, aromatic national drink of Peru and Chile.
items.story: Created in the early 20th century in Lima, Peru. The egg white gives it a beautiful foam, and the bitters create an aromatic finish. It's a South American classic that conquered the world and remains a sophisticated sour.
items.instructions: Dry shake pisco, lemon juice, simple syrup, and egg white. Add ice and shake hard. Strain into a rocks glass. Dash bitters on foam.

items.name: Between the Sheets
items.description: A seductive 1920s rum-cognac-orange classic.
items.story: A Prohibition-era favorite with a cheeky name. It combines rum and cognac with orange liqueur for a smooth, potent result. Popular in high-society circles, it remains a fun, historical cocktail with a wink.
items.instructions: Shake rum, cognac, triple sec, and lemon juice with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with orange twist.

items.name: White Lady
items.description: Harry Craddock's elegant gin-cointreau sour from the Savoy.
items.story: Created by the legendary Harry Craddock at the Savoy Hotel in London in the 1920s. A refined, sophisticated sour that became a favorite of high society. Clean, bright, and beautifully balanced — a true classic that still feels modern.
items.instructions: Shake gin, Cointreau, and lemon juice with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with lemon twist.

items.name: Bronx
items.description: A vibrant gin and orange juice classic from pre-Prohibition New York.
items.story: Created around 1906 at the Waldorf-Astoria in New York and named after the Bronx Zoo. It became one of the most popular cocktails of the early 20th century. The combination of gin and fresh orange juice makes it bright and approachable — a true taste of old New York sophistication.
items.instructions: Shake gin, sweet vermouth, dry vermouth, and orange juice with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with orange twist.

items.name: Ramos Gin Fizz
items.description: The famously frothy, shaken New Orleans gin fizz with cream and orange flower water.
items.story: Created in 1888 by Henry C. Ramos at the Imperial Cabinet in New Orleans. Famous for requiring a long, hard shake (traditionally up to 12 minutes). It became legendary during Mardi Gras and remains one of the most iconic — and labor-intensive — classics in cocktail history.
items.instructions: Dry shake all ingredients except soda. Add ice and shake very hard for a long time. Strain into a Collins glass and top slowly with soda.

items.name: Singapore Sling
items.description: The iconic pink gin sling from Raffles Hotel in Singapore.
items.story: Created around 1915 by Ngiam Tong Boon at the Long Bar in Raffles Hotel, Singapore. It became a global sensation and a symbol of tropical elegance. The combination of gin, cherry, and herbal notes makes it a beautiful, shareable classic.
items.instructions: Shake all ingredients with ice. Strain into a tall glass over ice. Garnish with cherry and orange wheel.

items.name: Blood and Sand
items.description: A smoky, sweet Scotch cocktail named after a 1922 film.
items.story: Created in the 1920s and named after the Rudolph Valentino film *Blood and Sand*. It beautifully balances smoky Scotch with sweet vermouth and cherry. A sophisticated, lesser-known classic that rewards Scotch lovers.
items.instructions: Shake Scotch, sweet vermouth, cherry liqueur, and orange juice with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with orange twist.

items.name: Casino
items.description: A beautiful pre-Prohibition gin sour with maraschino and bitters.
items.story: A 1917 classic from Hugo Ensslin's book. The maraschino and orange bitters give it a lovely complexity. It's an elegant, forgotten gem that deserves more attention — sophisticated and balanced.
items.instructions: Shake gin, maraschino liqueur, lemon juice, and orange bitters with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with cherry.

items.name: Ward Eight
items.description: A Boston whiskey sour with orange and grenadine.
items.story: Created in 1898 at the Locke-Ober in Boston to celebrate a political victory in Ward 8. It's a rich, fruity whiskey sour that was hugely popular in the early 20th century. A true piece of American political and cocktail history.
items.instructions: Shake whiskey, lemon juice, orange juice, and grenadine with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with cherry and orange.

items.name: Jack Rose
items.description: The beautiful pink applejack sour from the early 20th century.
items.story: Popular in the 1910s-1920s, the Jack Rose is one of the signature applejack cocktails. Its pink color comes from grenadine. It was a favorite of writers like Ernest Hemingway. A tart, elegant classic that highlights American apple brandy.
items.instructions: Shake applejack, lemon juice, and grenadine with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with lemon twist.

items.name: Monkey Gland
items.description: A daring 1920s gin-absinthe-orange cocktail from Paris.
items.story: Created by Harry MacElhone at Harry's New York Bar in Paris around 1920. Named after the controversial monkey gland rejuvenation experiments of the era. It's a fun, slightly scandalous classic that mixes gin with a touch of absinthe and orange.
items.instructions: Shake gin, orange juice, grenadine, and absinthe with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with orange twist.

items.name: Pink Lady
items.description: A pretty, egg-white gin sour with grenadine and applejack.
items.story: Popular in the 1920s-1930s, the Pink Lady is a beautiful, frothy gin cocktail. The egg white and grenadine give it a lovely pink color and silky texture. It was a favorite of the era's fashionable set and remains a charming, elegant classic.
items.instructions: Shake gin, applejack, lemon juice, grenadine, and egg white with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with cherry.

items.name: Stinger
items.description: A sharp, refreshing cognac and crème de menthe after-dinner drink.
items.story: Popular from the 1890s through the mid-20th century, the Stinger was a favorite of high society for its clean, minty finish. The name refers to the “sting” of the menthe. A simple, elegant digestif that still feels sophisticated today.
items.instructions: Stir cognac and white crème de menthe with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe or rocks glass over ice. Garnish with mint leaf.

items.name: Alexander
items.description: A rich, creamy cognac and crème de cacao after-dinner drink.
items.story: Popular in the early 20th century, the Alexander is a luxurious dessert cocktail. The combination of cognac, crème de cacao, and cream creates a silky, indulgent sip. Often served as a nightcap, it remains a timeless elegant classic.
items.instructions: Shake cognac, crème de cacao, and heavy cream with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with grated nutmeg.

items.name: Grasshopper
items.description: A vibrant green crème de menthe and chocolate dessert cocktail.
items.story: Created in the 1950s at Tujague's in New Orleans but with roots in earlier creamy cocktails. Its bright green color and mint-chocolate flavor made it a popular after-dinner drink. A fun, nostalgic classic that feels festive and indulgent.
items.instructions: Shake crème de menthe, crème de cacao, and heavy cream with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with grated chocolate or mint leaf.

items.name: Brandy Alexander
items.description: The brandy version of the creamy Alexander cocktail.
items.story: A popular variation of the Alexander, often served as a dessert or nightcap. It gained fame in the mid-20th century and was a favorite of many celebrities. Rich, smooth, and elegantly sweet — a true after-dinner classic.
items.instructions: Shake brandy, crème de cacao, and heavy cream with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with grated nutmeg.

items.name: Pink Squirrel
items.description: A pretty pink crème de noyaux and chocolate cream cocktail.
items.story: A mid-20th century American classic known for its pink color from crème de noyaux (almond liqueur). It was popular in supper clubs and remains a fun, nostalgic dessert drink with a retro charm.
items.instructions: Shake crème de noyaux, crème de cacao, and heavy cream with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with cherry.

items.name: Golden Cadillac
items.description: A luxurious Galliano, crème de cacao, and cream cocktail.
items.story: Created in the 1950s and named after the Cadillac car. The herbal Galliano gives it a unique vanilla-anise character. It was a popular dessert drink in the mid-century and remains a creamy, indulgent classic.
items.instructions: Shake Galliano, crème de cacao, and heavy cream with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe.

items.name: Grasshopper
items.description: The iconic bright green mint and chocolate cream cocktail.
items.story: Popularized in the 1950s at Tujague's in New Orleans. Its vibrant color and mint-chocolate flavor made it a favorite dessert drink. A fun, nostalgic classic that feels festive and playful.
items.instructions: Shake green crème de menthe, white crème de cacao, and heavy cream with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe.

items.name: White Russian
items.description: The creamy vodka, coffee liqueur, and cream classic.
items.story: Popularized in the 1970s but with roots in earlier Black and White Russians. Made famous by *The Big Lebowski*. A simple, indulgent after-dinner drink that feels both retro and timeless.
items.instructions: Build in a rocks glass over ice: vodka, coffee liqueur, then float cream on top. Stir gently.

items.name: Black Russian
items.description: The strong vodka and coffee liqueur predecessor to the White Russian.
items.story: Created in 1949 by a Belgian bartender in Brussels for a U.S. ambassador. Simple and potent, it became the base for the creamy White Russian. A true mid-century classic with a sophisticated edge.
items.instructions: Build in a rocks glass over ice: vodka and coffee liqueur. Stir gently.

items.name: Godfather
items.description: A smooth Scotch and amaretto nightcap.
items.story: Popularized in the 1970s and named after the famous film. The combination of Scotch and sweet almond amaretto creates a rich, easy-drinking digestif. A simple, masculine classic that feels luxurious.
items.instructions: Build in a rocks glass over ice: Scotch and amaretto. Stir gently.

items.name: Rusty Nail
items.description: The simple, bold Scotch and Drambuie classic.
items.story: Popular since the 1930s-1950s, the Rusty Nail is a straightforward mix of Scotch and the Scottish honey-herbal liqueur Drambuie. Its name comes from the rusty color. A true Scottish classic and a favorite nightcap for whisky lovers.
items.instructions: Build in a rocks glass over ice: Scotch and Drambuie. Stir gently.

items.name: Manhattan
items.description: The iconic New York whiskey and sweet vermouth classic.
items.story: Created in the 1870s at the Manhattan Club in New York. It quickly became a symbol of sophistication. The perfect balance of American whiskey and Italian vermouth makes it a cornerstone of cocktail history and a drink for all occasions.
items.instructions: Stir whiskey, sweet vermouth, and bitters with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with cherry.

items.name: Rob Roy
items.description: The Scotch version of the Manhattan.
items.story: Named after the Scottish folk hero Rob Roy MacGregor and created around the same time as the Manhattan. It showcases Scotch whisky beautifully with sweet vermouth and bitters. A sophisticated, smoky cousin to the Manhattan.
items.instructions: Stir Scotch, sweet vermouth, and bitters with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with cherry.

items.name: Boulevardier
items.description: The whiskey Negroni — bold and sophisticated.
items.story: Created in the 1920s for Erskine Gwynne's Paris magazine *The Boulevardier*. A whiskey lover's answer to the Negroni. It gained massive popularity during the modern cocktail renaissance and remains a favorite for its perfect balance.
items.instructions: Stir bourbon, Campari, and sweet vermouth with ice. Strain over a large ice cube. Garnish with orange twist.

items.name: Americano
items.description: The light, sparkling Campari and sweet vermouth aperitivo.
items.story: A classic Italian aperitivo from the early 20th century. It was the original base for the Negroni (before the gin was added). Refreshing and bittersweet, it's the perfect pre-dinner drink and a staple of Italian café culture.
items.instructions: Build in a tall glass over ice: Campari, sweet vermouth, and top with soda. Garnish with orange wheel.

items.name: Kir Royale
items.description: The festive Champagne and crème de cassis aperitif.
items.story: Named after Canon Félix Kir, a French priest and politician. The Royale version uses Champagne instead of white wine. A beautiful, elegant French classic that feels celebratory and sophisticated.
items.instructions: Pour crème de cassis into a flute and top with Champagne. Stir gently.

items.name: French 75
items.description: The sparkling gin and Champagne cocktail named after a WWI gun.
items.story: Created during World War I and named after the powerful French 75mm field gun because it “packs a serious punch.” A staple at the Savoy and a symbol of celebratory elegance ever since.
items.instructions: Shake gin, lemon juice, and simple syrup with ice. Strain into a flute and top with Champagne. Garnish with lemon twist.

items.name: Champagne Cocktail
items.description: The simple, elegant sugar cube and bitters Champagne drink.
items.story: A 19th-century classic that became a symbol of luxury. The bitters-soaked sugar cube adds complexity to the Champagne. It's one of the simplest yet most sophisticated ways to enjoy sparkling wine.
items.instructions: Place a sugar cube soaked in bitters in a flute. Top with Champagne. Garnish with lemon twist.

items.name: Mimosa
items.description: The classic Champagne and orange juice brunch cocktail.
items.story: Created in the 1920s in Paris and named after the mimosa flower. It became a worldwide brunch staple. Simple, refreshing, and celebratory — the perfect morning or afternoon drink.
items.instructions: Pour orange juice into a flute and top with Champagne. Stir gently.

items.name: Bellini
items.description: The famous Venetian peach and Prosecco cocktail.
items.story: Created in the 1940s by Giuseppe Cipriani at Harry's Bar in Venice. Named after the painter Giovanni Bellini because of its sunset color. A beautiful, elegant Italian classic that feels luxurious and summery.
items.instructions: Pour peach purée into a flute and top with Prosecco. Stir gently.

items.name: Kir
items.description: The classic French white wine and crème de cassis aperitif.
items.story: Named after Canon Félix Kir, a French priest and politician. The Royale version uses Champagne. A simple, elegant French tradition that remains a staple aperitif around the world.
items.instructions: Pour crème de cassis into a wine glass and top with chilled white wine. Stir gently.

items.name: Bijou
items.description: A jewel-like gin, sweet vermouth, and Chartreuse classic.
items.story: Created in the 1880s-1890s, the name 'Bijou' means jewel in French, referring to its colorful appearance. It combines gin, sweet vermouth, and green Chartreuse for a complex, herbal gem. A true pre-Prohibition beauty that rewards slow sipping.
items.instructions: Stir gin, sweet vermouth, and green Chartreuse with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with cherry.

items.name: Bamboo
items.description: A refined sherry and vermouth aperitif with Japanese influence.
items.story: Created in the 1880s-1890s in Yokohama, Japan, by a bartender at the Grand Hotel. It showcases dry sherry beautifully with vermouth and bitters. A sophisticated, underappreciated classic that feels both exotic and elegant.
items.instructions: Stir dry sherry, dry vermouth, and bitters with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with lemon twist.

items.name: Adonis
items.description: A sherry-based aperitif named after a Broadway play.
items.story: Created in the 1880s and named after the 1884 Broadway play *Adonis*. It highlights sweet sherry with vermouth and bitters. A beautiful, forgotten classic that deserves revival — sophisticated and easy to drink.
items.instructions: Stir sweet sherry, sweet vermouth, and bitters with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with orange twist.

items.name: Tuxedo
items.description: An elegant gin-absinthe-mar-aschino tuxedo cocktail.
items.story: Created in the late 19th century and named after the Tuxedo Park Club in New York. A sophisticated, dry gin cocktail with herbal notes. It's the perfect black-tie drink and a beautiful example of pre-Prohibition refinement.
items.instructions: Stir gin, dry vermouth, maraschino liqueur, and absinthe with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with cherry and lemon twist.

items.name: Improved Whiskey Cocktail
items.description: The upgraded 19th-century whiskey cocktail with maraschino and absinthe.
items.story: An evolution of the original Old Fashioned from the mid-19th century. The additions of maraschino and absinthe make it more complex and refined. A true historical gem that bridges the simple and the sophisticated.
items.instructions: Stir whiskey, simple syrup, maraschino liqueur, bitters, and absinthe with ice. Strain over a large ice cube. Garnish with lemon twist.

items.name: Sazerac
items.description: The official cocktail of New Orleans with rye and absinthe.
items.story: America's oldest cocktail, originating in the 1830s in New Orleans. Originally made with Cognac, it evolved to use rye whiskey. The absinthe rinse is iconic. A true piece of American cocktail history.
items.instructions: Rinse a chilled rocks glass with absinthe. Stir rye, sugar, and Peychaud's bitters with ice. Strain into the glass. Garnish with lemon twist.

items.name: Vieux Carré
items.description: The rich New Orleans rye-cognac-Benedictine classic.
items.story: Created in the 1930s at the Carousel Bar in New Orleans. It beautifully blends American rye with French cognac and herbal Benedictine. A true melting-pot cocktail that captures the spirit of the French Quarter.
items.instructions: Stir rye, cognac, sweet vermouth, Benedictine, and bitters with ice. Strain over a large ice cube. Garnish with cherry and lemon twist.

items.name: Improved Whiskey Cocktail
items.description: The enhanced 19th-century whiskey cocktail with maraschino and absinthe.
items.story: An evolution of the original Old Fashioned from the mid-19th century. The additions of maraschino liqueur and absinthe make it more complex and refined. A historical bridge between simple and sophisticated cocktails.
items.instructions: Stir whiskey, simple syrup, maraschino liqueur, bitters, and absinthe with ice. Strain over a large ice cube. Garnish with lemon twist.

items.name: Sazerac
items.description: New Orleans' official cocktail — rye with an absinthe rinse.
items.story: America's oldest cocktail, originating in the 1830s in New Orleans. Originally made with Cognac, it evolved to use rye whiskey. The absinthe rinse is iconic. A true piece of American cocktail history.
items.instructions: Rinse a chilled rocks glass with absinthe. Stir rye, sugar, and Peychaud's bitters with ice. Strain into the glass. Garnish with lemon twist.

items.name: Vieux Carré
items.description: The rich New Orleans blend of rye, cognac, and Benedictine.
items.story: Created in the 1930s at the Carousel Bar in New Orleans. It beautifully blends American rye with French cognac and herbal Benedictine. A true melting-pot cocktail that captures the spirit of the French Quarter.
items.instructions: Stir rye, cognac, sweet vermouth, Benedictine, and bitters with ice. Strain over a large ice cube. Garnish with cherry and lemon twist.

items.name: Harvard
items.description: A refined brandy and sweet vermouth cocktail with a touch of bitters.
items.story: Created in the late 19th century and named after Harvard University. It's a sophisticated cousin to the Manhattan, showcasing brandy instead of whiskey. A true Ivy League classic that feels both scholarly and celebratory.
items.instructions: Stir brandy, sweet vermouth, and bitters with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with lemon twist.

items.name: Yale
items.description: A dry gin cocktail with orange bitters and maraschino.
items.story: A pre-Prohibition classic named after Yale University. It's a sophisticated, dry gin drink with herbal and citrus notes. Part of the “Ivy League” cocktail family that celebrated East Coast elegance.
items.instructions: Stir gin, dry vermouth, maraschino liqueur, and orange bitters with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with lemon twist.

items.name: Princeton
items.description: A dry gin and port cocktail with orange bitters.
items.story: Another Ivy League classic named after Princeton University. It combines gin with a touch of port for color and depth. Elegant, dry, and refined — a perfect example of early 20th-century East Coast sophistication.
items.instructions: Stir gin, dry vermouth, and port with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with orange twist.

items.name: Chatham
items.description: A dry gin and herbal vermouth cocktail with a touch of Chartreuse.
items.story: A lesser-known but elegant pre-Prohibition gin cocktail. It highlights dry vermouth and herbal notes. Named after Chatham, it represents the refined, understated side of classic American cocktails.
items.instructions: Stir gin, dry vermouth, and green Chartreuse with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with lemon twist.

items.name: Seelbach
items.description: The bourbon Champagne cocktail with a heavy dose of bitters.
items.story: Discovered in the 1990s but dating back to the early 1900s at the Seelbach Hotel in Louisville. It combines bourbon with Champagne and a generous amount of bitters. A true hidden gem of American cocktail history.
items.instructions: Stir bourbon and bitters with ice. Strain into a flute and top with Champagne. Garnish with orange twist.

items.name: Remember the Maine
items.description: A bold rye, vermouth, and absinthe cocktail from the 1930s.
items.story: Created by Charles H. Baker Jr. in his 1939 book and named after the Spanish-American War rallying cry. It's a powerful, complex rye cocktail with a touch of absinthe. A true literary and historical classic.
items.instructions: Stir rye, sweet vermouth, Cherry Heering, and absinthe with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe.

items.name: Hanky Panky
items.description: Ada Coleman's famous gin, sweet vermouth, and Fernet Branca creation.
items.story: Created by Ada Coleman (head bartender at the Savoy Hotel) in the early 1900s for actor Charles Hawtrey. The name comes from his reaction: “By Jove! That is the real Hanky-Panky!” A bold, herbal classic that showcases Fernet Branca beautifully.
items.instructions: Stir gin, sweet vermouth, and Fernet Branca with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with orange twist.

items.name: Corpse Reviver No. 1
items.description: The original brandy-based hangover cure from the Savoy.
items.story: From the 1930 Savoy Cocktail Book. The “Corpse Reviver” family was designed as morning-after remedies. This No. 1 version is rich and apple-forward. A historical classic with a cheeky purpose.
items.instructions: Stir brandy, sweet vermouth, and Calvados with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe.

items.name: De La Louisiane
items.description: A rich New Orleans rye cocktail with Benedictine and absinthe.
items.story: A 1930s New Orleans classic from the St. Louis Hotel. It's a bolder, more complex cousin to the Vieux Carré. A true taste of Louisiana cocktail culture with herbal depth and rye power.
items.instructions: Stir rye, sweet vermouth, Benedictine, Peychaud's bitters, and absinthe with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with cherry.

items.name: Liberal
items.description: A bold whiskey cocktail with orange curaçao and bitters.
items.story: A pre-Prohibition classic that showcases American whiskey with a touch of orange and heavy bitters. Its name reflects a progressive spirit of the era. Strong, flavorful, and historically significant.
items.instructions: Stir whiskey, orange curaçao, and bitters with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with orange twist.

items.name: Aviation
items.description: A beautiful pre-Prohibition gin sour revived with violet liqueur.
items.story: Originally from Hugo Ensslin's 1916 book, lost for decades and revived during the modern cocktail renaissance. The violet liqueur gives it a stunning sky-blue hue. A true elegant classic that feels both historical and fresh — named for the new age of aviation.
items.instructions: Shake gin, maraschino liqueur, crème de violette, and lemon juice with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with cherry.

items.name: Hemingway Daiquiri
items.description: Ernest Hemingway's preferred drier, grapefruit-laced Daiquiri.
items.story: Hemingway's favorite at La Floridita in Havana. He liked it 'with no sugar and double rum.' The addition of maraschino and grapefruit makes it tart and complex. A true literary classic that remains a favorite among rum lovers.
items.instructions: Shake rum, maraschino liqueur, lime juice, and grapefruit juice with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with lime wheel.

items.name: Margarita
items.description: The iconic tequila, lime, and triple sec classic.
items.story: Popularized in the 1940s–1950s along the U.S.-Mexico border. The most famous tequila cocktail in the world. Simple, balanced, and endlessly customizable — the ultimate party and beach drink.
items.instructions: Shake tequila, triple sec, and lime juice with ice. Strain into a salt-rimmed rocks or coupe glass. Garnish with lime wheel.

items.name: Sidecar
items.description: The refined cognac, orange liqueur, and lemon classic.
items.story: Created in Paris during World War I and named after the motorcycle sidecar of an American officer. A symbol of elegance in the 1920s. The perfect balance of rich cognac and bright citrus makes it timeless.
items.instructions: Shake cognac, triple sec, and lemon juice with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe. Sugar rim optional.

items.name: White Lady
items.description: Harry Craddock's elegant gin-cointreau sour from the Savoy.
items.story: Created by Harry Craddock at the Savoy Hotel in the 1920s. A refined, sophisticated sour that became a favorite of high society. Clean, bright, and beautifully balanced — a true classic that still feels modern.
items.instructions: Shake gin, Cointreau, and lemon juice with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with lemon twist.

items.name: Between the Sheets
items.description: A seductive 1920s rum-cognac-orange classic.
items.story: A Prohibition-era favorite with a cheeky name. It combines rum and cognac with orange liqueur for a smooth, potent result. Popular in high-society circles and still fun today.
items.instructions: Shake rum, cognac, triple sec, and lemon juice with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with orange twist.

items.name: Corpse Reviver No. 2
items.description: The famous 'hair of the dog' hangover cure from the Savoy.
items.story: From the 1930 Savoy Cocktail Book. The recipe warns 'four of these taken in swift succession will un-revive the dead.' A perfectly balanced, complex classic that actually works as a morning pick-me-up.
items.instructions: Shake gin, Lillet Blanc, Cointreau, lemon juice, and absinthe with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with orange twist.

items.name: Last Word
items.description: The equal-parts Prohibition-era gem with chartreuse and maraschino.
items.story: Created around 1916 at the Detroit Athletic Club. Lost for decades and revived during the modern cocktail renaissance. The perfect harmony of four equal parts makes it a bartender favorite and a shining example of pre-Prohibition ingenuity.
items.instructions: Shake gin, lime juice, maraschino liqueur, and green Chartreuse with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with cherry.

items.name: Paper Plane
items.description: The equal-parts modern sour with Aperol and Amaro Nonino.
items.story: Created by Sam Ross in 2008. Named after the M.I.A. song “Paper Planes.” It quickly became a modern classic for its perfect balance of bitter and sweet. A brilliant, approachable cocktail that feels both new and timeless.
items.instructions: Shake bourbon, Aperol, Amaro Nonino, and lemon juice with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe.

items.name: Penicillin
items.description: The smoky Scotch sour with honey-ginger syrup.
items.story: Created by Sam Ross in New York in the early 2000s. It became one of the most influential modern classics, bridging smoky Scotch with bright citrus and sweet-spicy ginger. A true modern masterpiece.
items.instructions: Shake Scotch, lemon juice, honey-ginger syrup, and Islay Scotch float with ice. Strain over ice. Garnish with candied ginger.

items.name: Texas Manhattan
items.description: A bold Texan twist on the Manhattan using rye and local chili bitters.
items.story: Born in the modern Texas cocktail renaissance, this riff on the 19th-century Manhattan swaps in Texas rye and chili tincture to honor the Lone Star State's fiery spirit. New Yorkers appreciate the refined vermouth backbone while Texans love the smoky heat. The name nods to the classic while claiming Big Sky territory—bartenders tell guests it's 'where Wall Street meets the Alamo.'
items.instructions: Stir all ingredients with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with a brandied cherry and orange twist.

items.name: Big Apple Old Fashioned
items.description: A sophisticated NYC-smoked Old Fashioned with maple and apple notes.
items.story: A modern New York evolution of the 1800s Old Fashioned, created in Brooklyn bars during the craft revival. It layers smoked Texas bourbon with Big Apple cider syrup to bridge Southern smoke and Northern polish. The name celebrates New York as the 'Big Apple.' Guests love hearing how it evokes roaring 20s speakeasies with a Texas-sized pour.
items.instructions: Stir bourbon, syrup, and bitters with ice. Strain over a large ice cube in a rocks glass. Garnish with apple slice and expressed orange peel.

items.name: Lone Star Negroni
items.description: A Texan-strength Negroni with mezcal and grapefruit twist.
items.story: This modern classic fuses the 1919 Italian Negroni with Texas border influences. Bartenders in Austin and NYC experimented with mezcal for smoke and grapefruit for citrus pop. It represents the melting pot—Italian roots, Texan fire, New York edge. Tell guests it's 'strong enough to rope a steer and smooth enough for the skyline.'
items.instructions: Stir all ingredients with ice. Strain into a rocks glass over large ice. Garnish with grapefruit twist.

items.name: NYC Ranch Water
items.description: A refined New York take on the iconic Texan Ranch Water.
items.story: Originating on Texas ranches in the 20th century as a simple thirst-quencher, this modern classic exploded in popularity. New York bartenders elevated it with premium tequila and fresh lime. The name evokes wide-open Texas spaces meeting Manhattan high-rises. It's the ultimate crossover hit—bartenders say one sip and you're 'two-stepping in Times Square.'
items.instructions: Build in a highball glass with ice. Top with sparkling water. Garnish with lime wheel.

items.name: Brooklyn Bramble
items.description: A New York bramble with blackberry and Texas honey.
items.story: Evolved from the 1980s London Bramble, this version was popularized in Brooklyn bars. It adds Texas wildflower honey for sweetness and depth. Named after the borough that redefined modern classics. Guests adore the story of how it went from speakeasy secret to rooftop staple.
items.instructions: Shake gin, lemon, and honey with ice. Strain over crushed ice. Drizzle blackberry liqueur. Garnish with blackberries and mint.

items.name: Austin Avenue
items.description: A spicy Texan rum cocktail with New York polish.
items.story: Created in Austin's craft scene but refined in NYC, this modern classic blends Jamaican rum with ancho chili and citrus. It bridges Texas heat with New York elegance. The name references Austin's famous streets meeting Manhattan avenues. Bartenders love sharing how it captures the energy of both cities.
items.instructions: Shake all ingredients with ice. Double strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with ancho chili flake rim.

items.name: Hudson Highball
items.description: An elegant New York rye highball with Texan bitters.
items.story: A modern update to the classic highball, popularized along the Hudson River bars. It uses New York rye and Texas-made bitters for depth. Simple yet sophisticated—like a stroll through Central Park with cowboy boots. The perfect 'think Texan and New York' hybrid.
items.instructions: Build in a highball glass with ice. Top with soda. Garnish with lemon twist.

items.name: Alamo Sour
items.description: A Texan whiskey sour with egg white and chili heat.
items.story: Modern evolution of the 19th-century sour, born in Texas bars and embraced in New York. The egg white gives NYC-style silkiness while chili bitters bring Lone Star fire. Named for the iconic Texas fort. Guests always ask for the tale of its 'last stand' of flavor.
items.instructions: Dry shake all ingredients, then shake with ice. Double strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with chili thread.

items.name: Times Square Toddy
items.description: A hot modern classic toddy with Texas honey and New York spice.
items.story: Adapted from the 18th-century hot toddy for cold NYC winters, this version uses Texas whiskey and local honey. It warms both body and soul. The name evokes bright Times Square lights. Perfect fireside story: 'It'll light up your night like Broadway.'
items.instructions: Build in a mug: pour whiskey and honey, top with hot water. Stir. Garnish with clove-studded lemon wheel.

items.name: Border Boulevardier
items.description: A spicy Texan Boulevardier with rye and chili vermouth.
items.story: A modern Texas twist on the 1920s Boulevardier (a Negroni cousin). NYC bartenders embraced the ancho and rye for depth. It perfectly marries Texan boldness with New York refinement. The 'border' references the cultural crossroads. One of the best crossover modern classics.
items.instructions: Stir all ingredients with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with orange twist.

items.name: Dallas Daiquiri
items.description: A refined Texan daiquiri with chili rim and aged rum depth.
items.story: Modern evolution of the 1890s Cuban Daiquiri, embraced by Dallas bartenders who added local heat. It balances New York-style precision with Texas swagger. The name honors the city that made it famous in the craft era. Bartenders love telling guests it's ‘smooth as a Texas handshake, sharp as a Manhattan deal.'
items.instructions: Shake rum, lime, and syrup with ice. Double strain into a chilled coupe with chili-salt rim. Garnish with lime wheel.

items.name: Wall Street Whiskey Smash
items.description: A minty, lemony New York smash with Texas bourbon backbone.
items.story: Updated from the 19th-century Smash, this version thrives in NYC financial district bars using Texas bourbon for power. It captures the fast-paced energy of Wall Street with refreshing herbs. Guests smile when you say it's ‘the drink that closes deals and starts celebrations.'
items.instructions: Muddle mint and lemon in shaker. Add bourbon and syrup. Shake with ice. Double strain over crushed ice. Garnish with mint bouquet.

items.name: Austin Aviation
items.description: A Texan Aviation with crème de violette and grapefruit.
items.story: Modern take on the pre-Prohibition Aviation, reimagined in Austin with local citrus and Texas gin. New York bartenders appreciate its elegant violet hue. Named for the city that keeps innovating. It's the cocktail that flies high between Southern roots and big-city flair.
items.instructions: Shake all ingredients with ice. Double strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with brandied cherry.

items.name: SoHo Sour
items.description: A New York sour with Texas rye and red wine float.
items.story: Evolved from the classic New York Sour of the 1880s, this version uses Texas rye for backbone and a bold red wine float. Popular in SoHo lounges. It perfectly blends Manhattan sophistication with Lone Star strength. The story always lands: ‘classy enough for gallery openings, tough enough for the trail.'
items.instructions: Shake whiskey, lemon, and syrup with ice. Strain into coupe. Float red wine on top. Garnish with orange twist.

items.name: Rio Grande Rob Roy
items.description: A smoky Texan Rob Roy with peaty scotch and ancho.
items.story: Modern spin on the 1890s Rob Roy, created along the Texas border with a smoky twist. NYC bartenders fell in love with the ancho vermouth addition. It bridges Scottish heritage with Texan fire. Tell guests it's the drink that ‘flows strong from the Rio Grande to the Hudson.'
items.instructions: Stir all ingredients with ice. Strain into chilled coupe. Garnish with orange twist.

items.name: Brooklyn Buck
items.description: A dark rum buck with Texas ginger beer and lime.
items.story: Modern classic variation on the Moscow Mule family, popularized in Brooklyn with dark rum and fiery Texas ginger beer. It captures the vibrant energy of both cities. The name nods to the borough while honoring Texas spice. One of the most refreshing cross-country crowd-pleasers.
items.instructions: Build in highball with ice. Top with ginger beer. Garnish with lime wheel and mint.

items.name: Hill Country Hemingway
items.description: A Texan Hemingway Daiquiri with grapefruit and maraschino.
items.story: Inspired by Ernest Hemingway's favorite, this Texas Hill Country version amps up the grapefruit. Refined in New York bars for balance. It honors the writer's adventurous spirit with Lone Star soul. Bartenders tell guests it's ‘literary, strong, and full of character—just like Texas.'
items.instructions: Shake all ingredients with ice. Double strain into chilled coupe. Garnish with lime wheel.

items.name: Central Park Cobbler
items.description: A sherry cobbler with Texas berries and New York polish.
items.story: Revived from the 19th-century Sherry Cobbler, this version shines in Central Park picnics and Texas ranches alike. Fresh local berries meet fine sherry. It's the ultimate elegant summer sipper that feels right at home in both worlds.
items.instructions: Muddle berries in shaker. Add sherry, lemon, and syrup. Shake and pour over crushed ice. Garnish with mint and berries.

items.name: Fort Worth Flip
items.description: A rich Texan whiskey flip with port and nutmeg.
items.story: Updated from the colonial-era Flip, this Fort Worth favorite uses local whiskey and a touch of port. It gained traction in New York winter menus. Creamy, comforting, and strong — the perfect fireside story of Texas resilience meeting New York warmth.
items.instructions: Shake all ingredients with ice. Double strain into chilled coupe. Garnish with fresh grated nutmeg.

items.name: Empire State Espresso Martini
items.description: A caffeinated New York classic with Texas coffee liqueur.
items.story: The 1990s Espresso Martini exploded in NYC, and this version uses bold Texas cold-brew liqueur. It's the ultimate late-night energizer that bridges Manhattan nights and Austin energy. The name celebrates the Empire State. Bartenders call it ‘the drink that keeps the city (and the ranch) awake.'
items.instructions: Shake all ingredients with ice. Double strain into chilled coupe. Garnish with coffee beans.

items.name: San Antonio Sazerac
items.description: A Texan rye Sazerac with ancho absinthe rinse.
items.story: Modern Texas adaptation of the 1830s New Orleans Sazerac. San Antonio bartenders swapped in local rye and ancho chile for a fiery edge while keeping the absinthe elegance that New Yorkers adore. It's a beautiful border-meets-bayou story served with a chilled glass and big personality.
items.instructions: Rinse chilled rocks glass with absinthe. Stir rye, syrup, and Peychaud's with ice. Strain into glass. Garnish with lemon twist.

items.name: Harlem Honeysuckle
items.description: A floral New York gin cocktail with Texas wildflower honey.
items.story: Created in Harlem's vibrant cocktail scene and sweetened with Texas wildflower honey. It's a modern classic that feels like spring in Central Park with a Southern drawl. The name evokes the sweet energy of the neighborhood. Guests always want to know the secret behind that perfect floral lift.
items.instructions: Shake gin, lemon, honey, and liqueur with ice. Double strain into chilled coupe. Garnish with edible flower.

items.name: El Paso El Presidente
items.description: A bold Texan Presidente with aged rum and chili vermouth.
items.story: Updated from the 1920s Cuban Presidente, this El Paso version brings Texas spice and robust rum. It found fans in New York's Latin-inspired bars. The name celebrates the border city's vibrant culture. It's the kind of drink that tells stories of cross-cultural Cheers from El Paso to Manhattan.
items.instructions: Stir all ingredients with ice. Strain into chilled coupe. Garnish with orange twist.

items.name: Fifth Avenue Flip
items.description: A luxurious New York brandy flip with Texas pecan notes.
items.story: Revived from the golden age of flips, this Fifth Avenue version uses Texas brandy and pecan liqueur. It's the epitome of New York elegance with Southern warmth. Perfect for telling tales of old Manhattan while sipping something that feels like home on the range.
items.instructions: Shake all ingredients with ice. Double strain into chilled coupe. Garnish with fresh nutmeg.

items.name: Laredo Last Word
items.description: A Texan Last Word with mezcal and chartreuse heat.
items.story: Modern borderlands take on the 1916 Last Word. Laredo bartenders added mezcal and a touch of chili for Texas personality while keeping the equal-parts balance New Yorkers champion. It's equal parts sharp, smoky, and unforgettable.
items.instructions: Shake all ingredients with ice. Double strain into chilled coupe. Garnish with lime wheel.

items.name: Madison Square Mule
items.description: A refined New York mule with Texas ginger beer and jalapeño.
items.story: The iconic Moscow Mule, reimagined in Madison Square with premium Texas ginger beer and a subtle jalapeño kick. It's the drink that powers both Wall Street lunches and Austin happy hours. Refreshing, bold, and always a crowd favorite.
items.instructions: Build in copper mug with ice. Top with ginger beer. Garnish with lime and jalapeño slice.

items.name: Gulf Coast Gimlet
items.description: A coastal Texan gimlet with fresh lime and rosemary.
items.story: Updated from the classic British Gimlet, this Gulf Coast version uses Texas gin and rosemary from the coastal plains. It found a second home in New York seafood bars. Crisp, herbal, and evocative of sea breezes and Texas sunsets.
items.instructions: Shake gin, lime, and rosemary syrup with ice. Double strain into chilled coupe. Garnish with rosemary sprig.

items.name: Broadway Boulevardier
items.description: A New York Boulevardier with Texas bourbon and smoked orange.
items.story: The classic Boulevardier, brought to Broadway stages with Texas bourbon and a smoked orange twist. It's rich, bitter, and perfectly balanced — the drink that feels right before the curtain rises or after a long trail ride.
items.instructions: Stir all ingredients with ice. Strain over large ice in rocks glass. Garnish with smoked orange peel.

items.name: Palo Duro Paloma
items.description: A bold Texan Paloma with grapefruit and smoked salt.
items.story: The beloved Mexican Paloma, claimed by Texas with Palo Duro-inspired grapefruit and smoked salt. New York bars serve it as a sophisticated highball. Bright, salty, and endlessly drinkable — the taste of wide-open skies and city rooftops.
items.instructions: Build in highball with ice. Top with grapefruit soda. Garnish with grapefruit wheel and smoked salt rim.

items.name: Yankee Dandy
items.description: A refined brandy cocktail with Texas apricot and New York bitters.
items.story: Modern descendant of early American fancy drinks, this Yankee Dandy combines Texas apricot liqueur with classic New York bitters. It's elegant, fruity, and just a little bit rebellious — the perfect toast to both the Big Apple and the Lone Star.
items.instructions: Stir all ingredients with ice. Strain into chilled coupe. Garnish with apricot slice.

items.name: Vesper
items.description: James Bond’s iconic gin-vodka Lillet martini.
items.story: Created in 1953 by Ian Fleming in *Casino Royale* and named after the character Vesper Lynd. It blends British gin with Russian vodka and French Lillet for a perfectly balanced, sophisticated spy’s choice. Bartenders love telling guests this is the drink that made the Vesper famous: strong, dry, and unforgettable.
items.instructions: Shake gin, vodka, and Lillet with ice. Strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with lemon twist.

items.name: Negroni
items.description: The iconic equal-parts Italian bitter classic.
items.story: Invented in 1919 in Florence when Count Camillo Negroni asked for a stronger Americano. This beautiful ruby-red drink became a symbol of Italian aperitivo culture. It spread across Europe and the world. Bartenders always share that one sip transports you straight to a Florence terrace at sunset.
items.instructions: Stir gin, Campari, and sweet vermouth with ice. Strain over large ice in rocks glass. Garnish with orange twist.

items.name: Boulevardier
items.description: The whiskey Negroni — rich and sophisticated.
items.story: Created in the 1920s in Paris for American writer Erskine Gwynne. It’s the Boulevardier magazine namesake. This French-American hybrid became a European classic. Guests adore the story of how it replaced gin with bourbon for a deeper, more contemplative sip.
items.instructions: Stir bourbon, Campari, and sweet vermouth with ice. Strain over large ice. Garnish with orange twist.

items.name: Sidecar
items.description: The elegant French brandy and orange classic.
items.story: Born in Paris during World War I, supposedly named after an officer who arrived at a bar in a motorcycle sidecar. It became a staple of European high society. The perfect balance of sweet and sour makes it a timeless favorite that feels luxurious in every era.
items.instructions: Shake brandy, Cointreau, and lemon juice with ice. Double strain into chilled coupe. Garnish with orange twist.

items.name: Last Word
items.description: The equal-parts gin, lime, Chartreuse, and maraschino gem.
items.story: Created around 1916 at the Detroit Athletic Club but quickly became a European favorite. The name comes from the bartender’s boast that it was “the last word” in cocktails. Its perfect balance of sweet, sour, herbal, and spirit makes it one of the most beloved pre-Prohibition classics revived in modern times.
items.instructions: Shake all ingredients with ice. Double strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with brandied cherry.

items.name: White Lady
items.description: The refined gin sour with triple sec and egg white.
items.story: Created in the 1920s at London’s Ciro’s Club and later refined at the Savoy. A favorite of European high society. The egg white gives it a silky texture that feels luxurious. It’s often called the elegant cousin of the Sidecar.
items.instructions: Shake all ingredients with ice. Double strain into chilled coupe.

items.name: Bamboo
items.description: The dry sherry and vermouth classic from Yokohama.
items.story: Invented by German bartender Louis Eppinger at the Grand Hotel in Yokohama, Japan in the 1890s. It became a favorite across European diplomatic circles. A lighter, drier cousin to the Manhattan that showcases sherry beautifully.
items.instructions: Stir sherry, dry vermouth, and bitters with ice. Strain into chilled coupe. Garnish with lemon twist.

items.name: Corpse Reviver No. 2
items.description: The famous Savoy hangover cure.
items.story: From the 1930 *Savoy Cocktail Book*, this is the most popular of the Corpse Reviver family. Designed to ‘revive the dead’ the morning after. The absinthe float adds mystery. A true European classic still served in grand hotels across the continent.
items.instructions: Shake all ingredients with ice. Double strain into chilled coupe. Garnish with lemon twist.

items.name: Bijou
items.description: The jewel-toned gin, vermouth, and Chartreuse classic.
items.story: Created in the 1880s in the United States but quickly adopted across Europe. The name means ‘jewel’ in French, referring to its ruby, emerald, and diamond colors from the three spirits. A true gem of European cocktail culture.
items.instructions: Stir gin, sweet vermouth, and Chartreuse with ice. Strain into chilled coupe. Garnish with cherry.

items.name: Americano
items.description: The light, sparkling Italian aperitivo classic.
items.story: Born in the 1860s in Italy as a simpler, sparkling cousin to the Negroni. It was a favorite of American tourists — hence the name. Perfect for European aperitivo hour. Light, bitter, and refreshing — the drink that starts every great Italian evening.
items.instructions: Build in highball glass with ice. Top with soda water. Garnish with orange slice.
